clue.text: Post for men, by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the letters are those of a word heard, not written

parts.note: something for men is male

explanation.surface: A query about whether letters are delivered only to men, or something sounding similar.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE (for men) is said aloud and spelt as its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Post and mail are synonyms for letters and parcels delivered through the postal service.

clue.text: Unfortunate friar in A&E finding cost going up

indicators.note: in says the shuffled friar goes inside A&E

parts.note: A&E as written, its two letters

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the friar comes to grief and is jumbled

explanation.surface: An unlucky friar in hospital emergency discovers the bill climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's Accident and Emergency department. 'going up' means flying.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfare is the price of a ticket for a flight, the cost of travelling by air.

clue.text: With article removed, start meal

indicators.note: With opens the phrase telling us something is taken away
removed says the article is taken out of the word for start

parts.note: to launch is to start
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A meal starts once an item is taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunch is the midday meal.

clue.text: Account by cleric with no mistake

indicators.note: by here means placed next to, so the cleric follows the account

parts.note: a curate is an assistant member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A vicar's careful bookkeeping is error-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is correct and precise, free from any error.

clue.text: Mimic clumsy person

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an oafish, awkward person

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to imitate and, as a noun, a lumbering oaf.

clue.text: Record, very bad, extremely lame

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad

indicators.note: extremely means the extremes, first and last letters, of lame

parts.note: only the outer letters are used

explanation.surface: A dismal verdict on a record: terrible and painfully weak.
explanation.walkthrough: Chronic in British slang means dreadful, as in a chronic performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written historical account of events in order.

clue.text: Copy salesperson left I scan, removing covers

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative

indicators.note: removing covers strips the outer letters from scan

parts.note: only its middle letters are kept

explanation.surface: A salesperson leaves after photocopying and stripping off the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact reproduction of an original.

clue.text: Row about learner, one working on roof?

indicators.note: about says the row goes around the learner

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L is the learner plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: An argument about a trainee roofer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, an argument; it is really a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiler lays tiles, and roofs are a common place for that trade.

clue.text: Splendour of Greece and Europe half-forgotten?

parts.note: GR is the international vehicle code for Greece

indicators.note: half-forgotten means one half of the word is lost, so only its first half survives

parts.note: only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A wistful question about whether the glory of ancient Greece and Europe has faded from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-forgotten' keeps the first half of EUROPE; the question mark admits the continent is not really forgotten.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur is impressive magnificence, the same quality as splendour.

clue.text: Survey charge having payment at start for time

indicators.note: having introduces the change the charge undergoes
the payment letter takes the place of the time letter at the front of the word

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge
P is the abbreviation for payment

explanation.surface: A survey asking about a fee that must be paid up front.
explanation.walkthrough: TOLL loses its opening T, and P goes in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A poll is an opinion survey of a sample of people.

clue.text: Party in British wood

parts.note: ash is a hardwood tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A celebration held in a British woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: A bash is informal British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A bash is a lively social gathering or celebration, informally.

clue.text: Group, ill-willed at the outset, attempt robbery and violence

parts.note: a band is a group of people

indicators.note: at the outset means the opening letter of ill-willed is taken

parts.note: its first letter is used
try means attempt

explanation.surface: A malicious gang tries a spree of robbery and violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is the lawless activity of bandits: armed theft and violent crime.

clue.text: Obstruction bid — a racer confused

indicators.note: confused says these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled racer makes an attempt at something in the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a barrier set up to block passage.

clue.text: Nice drink, visiting bar at centre on return

indicators.note: on return says the letters are read backwards, right to left
visiting says the answer briefly stays within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: A pleasant drink in a bar in the middle of town, on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'bar at centre' backwards: ERTNECTARAB, and the answer sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods, so any delicious drink is called nectar.

clue.text: Annoyingly pester men caught in wrong legally

indicators.note: caught in says the men are held inside the legal wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Men caught doing something illegal and being nagged.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to harass and distress them persistently.

clue.text: Talk about empty lodge as holiday accommodation

indicators.note: about says the talk goes around the reduced lodge

parts.note: chat means talk

indicators.note: empty removes the inner letters of lodge, leaving just its first and last

parts.note: only its outside letters are kept

explanation.surface: Chatting about an unoccupied lodge used for holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' looks like describing a vacant lodge, but it strips the word's insides, leaving only its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, often in the mountains, rented by holidaymakers.

clue.text: A little water rat I classified as wandering

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A water rat being categorised by a naturalist as a roaming creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means moving irregularly without a fixed course, which is a wandering motion.

clue.text: Additional work due to unexpected item

parts.note: over can mean owing or outstanding, as a bill that is overdue

indicators.note: unexpected signals the letters of item turning up in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Extra hours worked because something surprising came up.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is time worked beyond normal hours, so extra labour on top of the usual.

clue.text: Watch Roman poet run off?

indicators.note: off says the run letter goes away from the poet's name

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet of the Aeneid
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Is the Roman poet out jogging?
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of keeping watch, often at night.

clue.text: Change theatrical act

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... is to change, as milk ...
second meaning: a performer's act or routine on stage

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to alter or become different and a short variety performance on stage.

clue.text: Workers group overlooking impudent talk in plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooking puts the workers group above the impudent talk

parts.note: TU is a trade union
lip is cheek, insolent talk

explanation.surface: A union ignores cheeky backchat in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking' looks like ignoring, but in a down answer it means sitting on top.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring-flowering bulb plant.

clue.text: Monster forgeries displayed regularly

indicators.note: displayed regularly means taking alternate letters, starting with the second

parts.note: every second letter of this word is used

explanation.surface: A villain shows off fake documents at intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a giant, cruel man-eating creature in folklore.

clue.text: Certain to use lab for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of these words are rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A scientist is sure about switching to a laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and beyond doubt, which is what certain means.

clue.text: For example, authority to influence decision?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: having a ... is a voice in a decision

explanation.definitionFit: The word introduces an instance, and as a noun means a right to be heard in decision-making.

clue.text: Praise, insincere, of place to live, too effusive, riling you initially

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a home

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.note: first letter used
first letter used
first letter used
first letter used

explanation.surface: Gushing compliments about your home annoy you.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat is the British word for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive compliments paid without sincerity, to win favour.

clue.text: Dad joining Church — step forward

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
CE stands for Church of England

explanation.surface: A father joining a congregation steps forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A pace is a single stride when walking.
